body_md:
Note that, the eventual surjectivity of $f^{\ast}$ implies the injectivity of $f$.  This point uses the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Chuseparated\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Chuseparated}}}).  Explicitly,
\begin{eqnarray}
\forall \sigma_A,\sigma'_A\in { \relax{S}}_{A},\;\; f(\sigma_A)=f(\sigma'_A) &\Leftrightarrow & (\,\forall { \relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\;\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}(f(\sigma_A))=\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}_B}(f(\sigma'_A))\,)\nonumber\\
&\Leftrightarrow & (\,\forall { \relax{l}}_B\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\;\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}}_B)}(\sigma_A)=\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{f^{\ast}({ \relax{l}}_B)}(\sigma'_A)\,)\nonumber\\
&\Leftrightarrow & (\,\forall { \relax{l}}'_B\in { \relax{E}}_{{ \relax{S}}_B},\;\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}'_B}(\sigma_A)=\epsilon^{{ \relax{S}}_B}_{{ \relax{l}}'_B}(\sigma'_A)\,)\nonumber\\
&\Leftrightarrow & (\, \sigma_A=\sigma'_A\,).
\end{eqnarray}
In the same way,  using the properties ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@Chuextensional\endcsname\@firstoftwo{Chuextensional}}}) and the eventual surjectivity of $f$, we can deduce the injectivity of $f^{\ast}$.

body_md:
\label{theoremcompletion}
We will assume that $({\relax{S}}',{ \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'),cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}},\star)$ is a real space of states.\\
We define ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ to be the set $cl^{{{ \relax{S}}'}}({ \mathcal{Q}}({ \relax{S}}'))$. The Inf semi-lattice structure being given by ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@RECdefJsqbarJ\endcsname\@firstoftwo{RECdefJsqbarJ}}}). We define the generalized space of effects as in Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defgeneralizedeffectspace\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defgeneralizedeffectspace}}} (it is necessary to use the formula for the suprema established in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@supremaJ\endcsname\@firstoftwo{supremaJ}}}) ). The reduced space of effects is defined as in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@reducedspaceofeffectsprime\endcsname\@firstoftwo{reducedspaceofeffectsprime}}}). Then, we define an evaluation map ${ \epsilon}^{{ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}}$ on the whole ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ as in ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@defepsilonS\endcsname\@firstoftwo{defepsilonS}}}).                                                                                                                                                                     
\\
As a result, ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ is a well defined space of states which admits the real structure $({{{ \relax{S}}'}},\star)$. The elements of ${{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ are the real states, whereas the elements of 
  ${ \relax{J}}_{{{ \relax{S}}'}}\smallsetminus {{{ \relax{S}}'}}$ are the hidden states.

label: orderimpliespolynomial
title: Lemma
body_md:
{\bf \@nx\protect\@empty\@nx\csname cite \endcsname[Theorem 1]{Fraser1978}}\label{orderimpliespolynomial}\\
Let us choose $\sigma_A,\sigma_{1,A},\cdots,\sigma_{n,A}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{A}}$ and $\sigma_B,\sigma_{1,B},\cdots,\sigma_{n,B}\in \overline{{ \relax{S}}_{B}}$. Then, 
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-2cm} \left( \bigsqcap{}^{{}^{{S}_{AB}}}_{1\leq i\leq n}\; \sigma_{i,A}\otimes \sigma_{i,B}\right) \sqsubseteq_{{}_{{S}_{AB}}} \sigma_{A}\otimes \sigma_{B}  \Leftrightarrow \nonumber\\  
&& (\,\textit{\rm there exists a n$-$ary lattice polynomial $p$}\;\vert\; \sigma_{A}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_A}}} p(\sigma_{1,A},\cdots,\sigma_{n,A})\nonumber\\
&&\textit{\rm and}\;\;  \sigma_{B}\sqsupseteq_{{}_{\overline{{ \relax{S}}_B}}} p^\ast(\sigma_{1,B},\cdots,\sigma_{n,B}) \,).
\end{eqnarray}
where $p^\ast$ denotes the lattice polynomial obtained from $p$ by dualizing the lattice operations.

body_md:
On ${\relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$, we will define the {\em consistency relation}, denoted $\asymp$                                                                 
, as follows (see Definition {{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@definwr\endcsname\@firstoftwo{definwr}}} for a definition of $\wr$):
\begin{eqnarray}
&&\hspace{-1cm}\forall \chi,\chi'\in {\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}},\;\;\;\;\chi \asymp \chi'\;\;:\Leftrightarrow\;\; (\,\chi=\chi'\;\;\textit{\rm or}\;\;\exists \epsilon\in \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\cap \Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi'),\;\;\epsilon=(\chi\sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\chi')\,)\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\\
&&\hspace{-1cm}\forall \chi\in {\check{\relax{S}}}\smallsetminus \overline{ \relax{S}},\forall \sigma\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\;\;\;\;\chi \asymp \sigma\;\;\Leftrightarrow\;\; \sigma \asymp \chi \;\;:\Leftrightarrow\;\; (\,\exists \epsilon\in\Theta^{\overline{ \relax{S}}}(\chi)\;\vert\; \epsilon \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{ \relax{S}}}}\sigma\,)\\
&&\hspace{-1cm}\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},\;\;\;\;\sigma \asymp \sigma'\;\;:\Leftrightarrow\;\; \sigma \wr \sigma'                                                                                                                                                                                                     
\end{eqnarray}
Note that, due to the property ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@coveringpropertySbar\endcsname\@firstoftwo{coveringpropertySbar}}}) we have $\forall \sigma,\sigma'\in \overline{ \relax{S}}{}^{{}^{pure}},(\sigma\sqcap_{{}_{\overline{\relax{S}}}}\sigma') \raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsupseteq$}}\,_{{}_{\overline{  \relax{S}}}}\sigma,\sigma'\;\textit{\rm or }\; \sigma=\sigma'$.

In other words, apart from the sheaf condition ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@VeblenYoung0\endcsname\@firstoftwo{VeblenYoung0}}}), we have proved the Veblen-Young's geometric axioms of projective spaces ({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@VeblenYoung3\endcsname\@firstoftwo{VeblenYoung3}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@VeblenYoung2\endcsname\@firstoftwo{VeblenYoung2}}})({{\rm\expandafter\@setref\csname r@VeblenYoung1\endcsname\@firstoftwo{VeblenYoung1}}}).

body_md: For any pair $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$, we define the line $\ell_{(\sigma_1\sigma_2)}$ to be the set of elements $\sigma_3$ in ${ \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that $\sigma_3=\sigma_1$ or $\sigma_3=\sigma_2$ or $\sigma_3\raisebox{1.3ex}{\,\rotatebox{180}{$\sqsubseteq$}}\,_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}(\sigma_1\sqcap_{{}_{{\relax{S}}}}\sigma_2)$.

title: Definition
body_md:
For any triple $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3\in { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ distinct, such that $\sigma_i\notin \ell_{(\sigma_j\sigma_k)}$ for any $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$, we define the plane $\wp_{(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)}$ to be the set of elements $\sigma_4$ in ${ \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ such that there exists $i,j,k$ with $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$ and 
$\lambda\in { \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ and $\lambda\in \ell_{(\sigma_i\sigma_4)}$ and $\lambda\in \ell_{(\sigma_j\sigma_k)}$. \\
The set of planes on ${ \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ will be denoted $\wp^{\check{\relax{S}}}$.\\
Any element of $\wp^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ has a structure of a projective sheaf.

Any plane is stable under the application of the third Veblen-Young's property.  In other words,  if there exists $U\in { elax{E}}^{\check{elax{S}}}$ and $\lambda, \sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in { elax{G}}^{\check{elax{S}}}$ such that $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\in U$  and such that ${elax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ and ${elax{r}}^U(\lambda,\sigma_3,\sigma_4)$ and $ orall \mu,
u,ho\in \{\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4\}, \;
eg\; {elax{r}}^U(\mu,
u,ho)$. Then,   $\lambda,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3,\sigma_4$ are in a same plane $\wp$. Moreover, if we introduce $U'\in { elax{E}}^{\check{elax{S}}}$ and the element $\mu\in U'$  such that ${elax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_1,\sigma_3)$ and ${elax{r}}^{U'}(\mu,\sigma_2,\sigma_4)$, and if we introduce  $U''\in { elax{E}}^{\check{elax{S}}}$

$\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_1}=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta$, $\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_2}=\alpha^\star\widetilde{\otimes}\beta$, $\Upsilon^{(j,k)}_{\sigma_3}=\alpha\widetilde{\otimes}\beta^\star$.

we say that the plane $\wp_{(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)}$ is a {\em starred plane}. The set of starred planes on ${ \relax{G}}^{\check{\relax{S}}}$ will be denoted $\wp_\star^{\check{\relax{S}}}$.
